description: Full MHFE suite 3 operations at the defaults (2 GiB, 12 passes, PIM 0) with the public zero-12 test vector: one encryption including its 12-round check (24 Argon2id calls) and one recovery (12 calls). One laptop; observations, not guarantees or attack-cost estimates.
method: Command line: `mhfe test-benchmark` of the release builds of commit ac195e8373df24fb11a1b0b241a324575ea09b03, the default one and the one built with --features ssse3.

Browser: headless Chromium through Playwright, driving the MHFE panel of the Wallet Key Derivation Tool (MHFE 0.4.0 browser package) twice: served by its executable version with COOP/COEP (fast mode, four threads) and opened as a file (standard mode, one thread). A fresh browser for each run.

Each run was followed by a 90-second pause. The main series ran twice, with the two command-line builds in swapped order in the second round; the first series was stopped after one round to add the SSSE3 build and is kept as an extra sample.

runs.argon2_engine: reference C, opt.c with SSE2, 4 threads
reference C, opt.c with SSSE3, 4 threads

runs.scenario: chromium, served by the executable (fast mode)

runs.argon2_engine: reference C, opt.c with SSSE3, 4 threads
reference C, opt.c with SSE2, 4 threads

runs.scenario: chromium, served by the executable (fast mode)

runs.argon2_engine: reference C, opt.c with SSE2, 4 threads

runs.scenario: chromium, served by the executable (fast mode)

findings: Command line: a recovery took 67 to 72 seconds, an encryption with its check 119 to 136 seconds. The SSSE3 build was 7 to 10 percent faster than the default build in both orders.
Browser fast mode: a recovery took 90 to 95 seconds, an encryption 160 to 168 seconds, about a quarter slower than the command line.
Browser standard mode: a recovery took 234 to 239 seconds, an encryption 459 to 479 seconds, 2.6 to 2.9 times the fast mode.
The one slower command-line recovery (84 seconds) started with the processor at 77 °C instead of 55 to 62 °C.
